facts.text: Pan's Labyrinth (2006, dir. Guillermo del Toro) won three Academy Awards at the 79th Academy Awards: Best Art Direction (Eugenio Caballero, Pilar Revuelta), Best Cinematography (Guillermo Navarro) and Best Makeup (David Martí, Montse Ribé).
Pan's Labyrinth also won three BAFTA Awards, including Best Film Not in the English Language, plus the Hugo Award for Best Dramatic Presentation, Long Form; it grossed about $83 million worldwide.

Pan's Labyrinth (Mexico, Spanish-language) was also nominated at the 79th Academy Awards for Best Foreign Language Film, Best Original Screenplay (del Toro) and Best Original Score (Javier Navarrete), but won only its three technical awards.

Sweeney Todd: The Demon Barber of Fleet Street (2007, dir. Tim Burton) won the Golden Globe for Best Motion Picture - Musical or Comedy and Johnny Depp won the Golden Globe for Best Actor - Musical or Comedy at the 65th Golden Globes.
Sweeney Todd received three Oscar nominations at the 80th Academy Awards (Best Actor for Johnny Depp, Costume Design, Art Direction) and won Best Art Direction.

Let the Right One In (2008, Sweden, dir. Tomas Alfredson) won four Guldbagge Awards (including Best Director, Best Cinematography and Best Screenplay), the Tribeca Founders Award for Best Narrative Feature, the Saturn Award for Best International Film and the Empire Award for Best Horror Film.
Let the Right One In was nominated for Best Film Not in the English Language at the 63rd British Academy Film Awards; an American remake, Let Me In, followed in 2010.

The Others (2001, dir. Alejandro Amenabar) earned 15 nominations at the 16th Goya Awards and won eight, including Best Film, Best Director and Best Original Screenplay - the first English-language film without Spanish dialogue to win Best Film at the Goyas.

The Others won three Saturn Awards at the 28th ceremony (Best Horror Film, Best Actress for Nicole Kidman, Best Supporting Actress for Fionnula Flanagan); Kidman was nominated for a Golden Globe (Best Actress - Drama) and a BAFTA for it.
The Ring (2002) won Best Horror Film and Best Actress (Naomi Watts) at the 29th Saturn Awards.
Saw (2004) was nominated for Best Horror Film at the 31st Saturn Awards.

I Am Legend (2007, dir. Francis Lawrence, starring Will Smith) grossed $585,532,684 worldwide, ranking No. 3 on Wikipedia's list of highest-grossing horror films (behind It (2017) and The Sixth Sense (1999)) - the highest of any 2000s horror release.

I Am Legend opened to $77.2 million in December 2007, the highest December opening weekend at the time, beating The Lord of the Rings: The Return of the King, until The Hobbit: An Unexpected Journey (2012).

Among 2000s releases on Wikipedia's highest-grossing horror list, M. Night Shyamalan's Signs (2002) grossed $408,250,578 worldwide (No. 11), Hannibal (2001) $351,692,268 (No. 16) and Van Helsing (2004) $300,157,638 (No. 25).

Paranormal Activity (shot for $15,000 by Oren Peli) had a limited US release on September 25, 2009 and a nationwide release on October 16, 2009; it grossed $194,183,034 worldwide and is often cited as the most profitable film ever by return on investment.

Paramount acquired the Paranormal Activity US rights from Peli for $350,000 and shot a new ending costing an additional $200,000; in its first full wide weekend it took No. 1 with $21.1 million from 1,945 theaters, beating Saw VI.
Saw (2004) was made for roughly $1-1.2 million and topped its opening weekend, grossing about $104 million worldwide ($103,911,669 on the list).

The Saw franchise (10 films to date) has grossed $1,141,842,812 worldwide, the fifth-highest-grossing horror franchise; Saw III (2006) is its top earner at $164,874,275, followed by Saw II (2005, $152,925,093) and Saw IV (2007, $139,352,633).
Guinness named Saw 'the most successful horror franchise in history' in 2010.

The Ring (2002) grossed $249.3 million worldwide on a $48 million budget, opening to $15 million on 1,981 screens and becoming a sleeper hit with $129.1 million in the US; its sequel The Ring Two (2005) grossed $163,995,949.

In the Final Destination series, The Final Destination (2009) grossed $187,384,627, Final Destination 3 (2006) $118,890,272, the first film (2000) $112,880,294 and Final Destination 2 (2003) $90,941,129.

The Final Destination (2009) is the highest-grossing film of the original run of the series at $187,384,627; Final Destination 3 (2006) grossed $118,890,272, the first film (2000) $112,880,294 and Final Destination 2 (2003) $90,941,129.

The Resident Evil film series passed $1.2 billion and was once the highest-grossing horror and video-game film series; the original series' six films total $1,237,978,176, led by The Final Chapter ($314,101,190).

Remakes at the box office: The Texas Chainsaw Massacre (2003) opened to $29.1 million and grossed $107.4 million worldwide on a $9.5 million budget; Dawn of the Dead (2004) opened to $27.3 million and grossed $102.3 million; Halloween (2007) grossed $80.4 million on a $15 million budget.

Remakes at the box office: The Texas Chainsaw Massacre (2003) opened to $29.1 million and grossed $107.4 million worldwide on a $9.5 million budget; Dawn of the Dead (2004) opened to $27.3 million and grossed $102.3 million; Halloween (2007) grossed $80.4 million.

The Saw films were released every October in the US: Saw (Oct 29, 2004, dir. James Wan), Saw II (Oct 28, 2005, Darren Lynn Bousman), Saw III (Oct 27, 2006), Saw IV (Oct 26, 2007), Saw V (Oct 24, 2008, David Hackl), Saw VI (Oct 23, 2009, Kevin Greutert).

Saw was created by James Wan and Leigh Whannell, premiered at Sundance on January 19, 2004 before its October 29, 2004 release by Lions Gate, and follows serial killer John 'Jigsaw' Kramer (Tobin Bell).

Final Destination (2000) was based on an unused spec script by Jeffrey Reddick originally written for The X-Files; the 2000s entries are Final Destination (2000), Final Destination 2 (2003), Final Destination 3 (2006) and The Final Destination (2009, dir. David R. Ellis).

The Resident Evil films, based on Capcom's games, star Milla Jovovich as the film-original Alice: Resident Evil (2002, Paul W. S. Anderson), Apocalypse (2004, Alexander Witt) and Extinction (2007, Russell Mulcahy).
Hostel (2005) was written and directed by Eli Roth and executive produced by Quentin Tarantino among others; it follows American tourists in Slovakia.
Underworld (2003, dir. Len Wiseman in his feature debut, starring Kate Beckinsale as Selene) grossed $95.7 million on a $22 million budget and launched a franchise about vampires and lycans.

The Ring (2002, dir. Gore Verbinski, written by Ehren Kruger) is a remake of the 1998 Japanese film Ring, based on Koji Suzuki's 1991 novel, and its success inspired American remakes of other Asian horror films.
The Grudge (2004) was directed by Takashi Shimizu, remaking his own 2002 Japanese film Ju-On: The Grudge; it stars Sarah Michelle Gellar and was produced by Sam Raimi.
Dark Water (2005, dir. Walter Salles, starring Jennifer Connelly) remakes Hideo Nakata's 2002 Japanese film Dark Water, based on Koji Suzuki's short story 'Floating Water'.
Pulse (2006, dir. Jim Sonzero, co-written by Wes Craven, starring Kristen Bell) is an English-language adaptation of Kiyoshi Kurosawa's 2001 Japanese film Pulse.
The Texas Chainsaw Massacre (2003) was directed by Marcus Nispel (feature debut), produced by Michael Bay, and remade Tobe Hooper's 1974 film; Nispel also directed the 2009 Friday the 13th reboot.
Dawn of the Dead (2004) was directed by Zack Snyder in his feature debut from a James Gunn screenplay, remaking George A. Romero's 1978 film, with Sarah Polley and Ving Rhames.
Rob Zombie wrote and directed Halloween (2007), a remake of John Carpenter's 1978 film and the ninth Halloween film, with Malcolm McDowell as Dr. Loomis and Tyler Mane as Michael Myers.

Friday the 13th (2009) is a reboot and the twelfth film in the franchise, with Jared Padalecki and Derek Mears as Jason Voorhees; The Last House on the Left (2009, dir. Dennis Iliadis) remakes Wes Craven's 1972 film and opened to $14.1 million.
